{"self_assessment": "Impact: The body held together well. Priya and Maya laid it nose to tail, and Leo's dorsal fin is joined. My part was the tail, which is what makes the fish readable, and it was only partly done at the push. The upper arm was nearly down and Leo was still laying the lower arm, so the tail was probably incomplete. I'd call our result a partial picture, not a clear fish.

Execution: My biggest mistake was laying the tail from the tip instead of from the arms. Priya caught it, and the redo cost us most of the last ten minutes. I also told the table 'the tail's down' and 'I'll call it when it's standing' before it was true, which had people waiting on me and checking joins that weren't ready. I should have checked the direction against the pad before placing a single domino.

Collaboration: Priya and Maya were patient and specific. Their join checks and Maya's nudge at the bottom edge were the best saves on the table. Leo took the lower arm when I asked and kept a clear inspection running. I could have handed off part of the tail sooner, once I could see I was falling behind.

Leadership: I didn't lead the tail well. I kept promising updates instead of giving concrete ones, and I didn't take up the offers of help from Priya and Leo until late. Next time I'd settle the build direction before the first domino goes down, give status in plain words, and ask for hands early, not when the clock forces it."}
